title: Learning Is Misunderstood
heading: Learning Is Misunderstood
coreClaim: The chapter argues that people often mistake easy, familiar-feeling study for real learning even though durable learning usually requires harder forms of recall, spacing, and variation.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is the split between fluency and durable retention: some strategies feel smooth because the material is present, while better strategies force reconstruction after some forgetting or discrimination among similar options.
requiredAnchors: Rereading and highlighting can create confidence without reliable later recall.
Massed practice and cramming often boost short-run fluency more than long-run retention.
Retrieval, spacing, and interleaving feel harder because they require effortful reconstruction and discrimination.
commonMisreadings: Any difficult study method must be good.
Passive review is always worthless rather than limited.
specificApplications: Use blank-page recall instead of another passive reread.
Space practice over time rather than compressing it into one block.
Mix similar problem types so the learner must choose the right tool.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep the line between desirable difficulty and pointless struggle explicit.
thresholdQuestion: What turns a hard-feeling study method into a productive learning mechanism instead of wasted friction?
